request.goal: Minimize the source's peak_allocated_bytes for the offline batch-32 workload while retaining images_per_second >= 0.95 of the original baseline, preserving its pretrained model, real image inputs, FP32 numerical policies, full logits and exact predicted classes. Keep the original workload and completion boundary.
notes: Command provenance: user command 'python resnet_inference.py --assets /root/autodl-tmp/dev/v6-work/validation-assets/resnet18 --output /tmp/original-resnet-memory'; with no overrides, common.py arguments() defaults apply: --workloads workloads.json, --warmup 2, --repeats 5, --profile off.
Selected workload row is resnet_inference.workloads[1] (id=offline, batch=32) copied verbatim from workloads.json:15-23; the online batch=1 row and held-out unseen_batch=7 are not part of this task.

peak_allocated_bytes is torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() read after torch.cuda.synchronize() in each repeat (resnet_inference.py:42-48), with reset_peak_memory_stats() before each sample: the process's PyTorch CUDA allocated peak, not reserved, whole-GPU or driver/NCCL memory. common.py summarize() reports median/min/max over the 5 repeats.

images_per_second = batch * 1e9 / elapsed_ns for one full batch-32 forward on the fixed GPU-resident input (resnet_inference.py:48) - full-request throughput for this workload, not cached-only throughput; constraint images_per_second >= 0.95 x original baseline median is the source notation images_per_second_min_baseline_ratio: 0.95.

Quality boundary: full 1000-class logits compared with torch.testing.assert_close at atol=rtol=1e-4 (workloads.json correctness logits_atol/logits_rtol); discrete output requiring exact comparison is the top-1 predicted classes: torch.equal(actual.argmax(-1), reference.argmax(-1)) plus predicted_labels via model.config.id2label (resnet_inference.py:31-35, workloads.json require_exact_top1). Reference semantics follow the source's saved offline-reference.pt (pixels + logits).

Numerical policy preserved: FP32 weights and activations (dtype=torch.float32 at resnet_inference.py:23), TF32 disabled for matmul and cudnn, cudnn.benchmark off, float32_matmul_precision 'highest', torch.manual_seed(20261020), 4 CPU threads (common.py configure(), resnet_inference.py:21).

Input construction: images[torch.arange(32, device='cuda') % len(images)].contiguous() from pixels.npy (3 real preprocessed public images, float32 NCHW 3x224x224), GPU-resident before timing; preprocessing was completed in the asset-preparation stage (prepare_resnet_assets.py), not in the measured work.

Single-process single-GPU workload: configure(device=0)/set_device and model.cuda(); no NCCL, no distributed backend, no communication collector fields required; the worker binds the leased GPU UUID (2x RTX 4090 present, this workload requires 1).

profile_once (torch.profiler trace) is a diagnostic run separate from clean timing in the source and was not requested by this goal; the objective is the ordinary evaluator metric peak_allocated_bytes from the clean sample loop, not a diagnostic collector field.

One measured invocation: One batch-32 inference invocation: infer(model, pixels) at resnet_inference.py:14-16, i.e. ResNetForImageClassification forward model(pixel_values=pixels).logits under @torch.inference_mode() on the fixed GPU-resident FP32 tensor of 32 preprocessed real images built at resnet_inference.py:29, ending at torch.cuda.synchronize() with the full 1000-class logits returned. Model loading, host->device input transfer, reference construction, correctness checks, warmup, statistical repeats and profiling are harness, not the repeated work.

selection.rationale: Objective is peak_allocated_bytes (baseline 280,169,472 B, median of clean samples) with images_per_second >= 0.95x7535.66 = 7158.9. The peak decomposes exactly from the measured assets: live FP32 params 46,758,048 + GPU-resident input 19,267,584 + conv1 output 32x64x112x112x4 = 102,760,448 coexisting with the out-of-place batch_norm1 output of the same size + 8,622,944 workspace = 280,169,472 exactly. That coexistence happens inside ResNetEmbeddings (model.resnet.embedder): the stem's two 112x112x64 tensors are 73% of the peak. Note the separately observed ReLU duplication (all 17 ReLUs out-of-place) is not the binding term: the ReLU moment is also a 2x102,760,448 coexistence, so in-place ReLU alone cannot move the peak; the conv->BN output coexistence is the floor that must be attacked. Selection: the stem region (ResNetEmbeddings module and its subtree: stem ResNetConvLayer 0022893ec8c1ceea869f with the single target model.resnet.embedder.embedder, its Conv2d/BatchNorm2d/ReLU modules, and the MaxPool2d pooler). The candidate replaces the ResNetEmbeddings forward (module boundary, children invoked through context.references; no functional dispatch sites, so the legacy direct-callable backend applies) to micro-batch the stem along the frozen batch dimension: 4 contiguous chunks of 8 rows, each chunk running the unchanged conv1 -> bn1(eval) -> relu1 -> maxpool path on a contiguous slice (no copies), with chunk outputs assembled into the same [32,64,56,56] hidden state (25,690,112 B) for the untouched stages. All inherited stem calls still execute (4x per invocation), preserving quality coverage without CUDA-graph replay. Region scope because every call in the stem subtree changes execution (invocation count 1->4, per-call batch 32->8); all 17 observed stem-subtree calls are listed, including the aten conv2d/batch_norm/relu/max_pool2d calls and the discovery record_function hooks that will fire per chunk. No calls outside the region are affected: stage 0+ receive the same-shape, same-value hidden state through the same ops. Rejected alternatives: whole-model micro-batching (execution_plan) would cut deeper (~122 MB) but re-times all 20 convs (~4156 us of diagnostic CUDA time) at batch 8 and risks the 7158.9 img/s floor; deduplicating the 3 unique input images contradicts the frozen batch-32 workload (all 32 rows must execute); CUDA-graph replay skips Python hooks and breaks coverage per binding-contract; folding BN into conv weights changes parameter values (invariant); in-place ReLU alone does not move the 2-tensor peak. Throughput safety: the stem is 907.7/4156.2 us (21.8%) of diagnostic CUDA time, and its kernels are bandwidth-bound on the 112x112x64 tensors - bn_fw_inf_1C11_NCHW 227.2 us, clamp/relu 217.8 us, max_pool_forward_nchw 198.7 us - whose grids stay far above SM saturation at batch 8 and whose total bytes moved are unchanged; only conv1's scudnn kernel (262.5 us) can lose modest efficiency, so even a 20% stem slowdown keeps wall time <= ~4.42 ms (>= ~7240 img/s).
selection.hypothesis: Chunking the stem 4x8 lowers peak_allocated_bytes from 280,169,472 B to approximately 143-152 MB (-46% to -49%). With batch-8 chunks the stem transient becomes params 46,758,048 + input 19,267,584 + assembled stem output 25,690,112 + one chunk's conv_out + bn_out coexistence 2x25,690,112 (+ small workspaces) = 143,095,968 + ws, which matches the new binding tier set outside the region by stage 0's out-of-place conv coexistence (input 25,690,112 + conv_out + bn_out), the eager-execution floor reachable without editing stage semantics. If measurement shows batch-8 chunks cost more than the 5% throughput budget, 2x16 chunks inside the same region still yield ~168.8 MB + ws (-38% to -40%); chunk size is tunable within this one boundary. Expected images_per_second 7300-7500 (>= 7158.9) since the bandwidth-bound stem kernels move identical total bytes at near-identical efficiency; expected numerics unchanged: identical aten kernels on contiguous batch slices, BN(eval)/ReLU/MaxPool per-sample exact, conv1 at worst reduction-order-level differences far below the atol=rtol=1e-4 logits tolerance, preserving exact top-1. These benefit, throughput and numerics expectations are hypotheses to be tested by the evaluator's clean timing, peak and quality checks.

proposal.rationale: Single replacement of the stem module boundary model.resnet.embedder (ResNetEmbeddings, group 3821cceac23fa97e5a55) per selection.json: an eager composite that micro-batches the frozen batch-32 request along the batch dimension. Baseline peak_allocated_bytes 280,169,472 B decomposes exactly as live FP32 params 46,758,048 + GPU-resident input 19,267,584 + out-of-place conv1 output 102,760,448 coexisting with the equally sized out-of-place batch_norm1 output + 8,622,944 workspace, all inside the stem; the parallel ReLU moment is the same 2x102,760,448 coexistence, so only attacking the conv->BN tier moves the peak. The replacement slices the contiguous [32,3,224,224] input into contiguous row chunks (no copies, no deduplication - all 32 rows execute), runs the unchanged sub-chain by calling the current parents through context.references (ResNetConvLayer 1dcfd07639d32233c49eafdf: conv2d->BatchNorm2d(eval)->ReLU; then MaxPool2d babacb997a72996bf303d028), assembles chunk results into one preallocated [32,64,56,56] tensor (25,690,112 B) and returns it to the untouched encoder stages - same shape, layout and values. No module.forward wrapper is installed by the candidate, no functional sites are declared, so the legacy direct-callable backend applies with no unrelated dispatch cost. Memory accounting at chunk 8: stem-internal peak = 46,758,048 + 19,267,584 + assembled output 25,690,112 + one chunk's conv_out + bn_out (2x25,690,112) = 143,095,968 B + workspaces, below the tier the unchanged stages set anyway. Honest expectation, correcting the selection's 143-152 MB estimate which omitted the second convolution's BatchNorm moment in stage 0: ResNetBasicLayer keeps residual (25,690,112) + layer[0] ReLU output (25,690,112) + layer[1] conv output (25,690,112) + layer[1] bn output (25,690,112) = 102,760,448 coexisting, so the post-optimization binding tier is 46,758,048 + 19,267,584 + 102,760,448 = 168,786,080 B (layer2.0 ties it: 25,690,112 + 6x12,845,056 = 102,760,448). Expected measured peak ~169-178 MB (tier + 3x3-conv workspaces), i.e. roughly -37% vs baseline; this is a hypothesis for the evaluator's clean samples, not a measured fact. Throughput: baseline median 7535.66 img/s (4.2465 ms), floor 7158.9 img/s (4.470 ms), headroom +224 us. Stem diagnostic CUDA time is 907.7/4156.2 us; its dominant kernels (bn_fw_inf 227.2 us, clamp/ReLU 217.8 us, max_pool 198.7 us) are bandwidth-bound with grids >=6272 blocks at batch 8 on the 128-SM 4090 and move identical total bytes, conv1's scudnn (262.5 us, grid 3136) may lose modest efficiency, plus ~15 extra launches, 4 assembly copies (25.7 MB total round-trip) and ~8 extra Python parent calls; even a 20% stem slowdown stays above 7158.9 img/s. Numerics: BatchNorm2d eval, ReLU and MaxPool2d are per-sample and value-exact under row chunking; conv2d is the identical aten op on contiguous slices with at most kernel-selection/reduction-order ulp effects far below the logits atol=rtol=1e-4, and a CPU replica of this exact composition is bit-identical to the parent stem. Coverage and contract: every inherited stem call still executes on each invocation (conv-layer and pooler subtrees 4x per invocation through context.references, their aten children and discovery record_function hooks firing per chunk); nothing is eliminated; no CUDA Graph capture or replay (replay would skip Python hooks and break runtime coverage per binding-contract); no state, caches or fixture-dependent outputs are retained - stateless eval-mode inference recomputes from the live input every call, with the framework's synchronize boundaries and the whole project measured unchanged. Guards: the chunked path applies only to the observed compatible signature (4-D cuda float32 contiguous 3-channel non-requires-grad input, batch > chunk, eval mode); anything else, kwarg-only calls, and any runtime exception inside the chunked path fall back to the parent reference with distinct record_route labels (stem_microbatch_rowsN / stem_single_chunk / stem_parent_signature_fallback / stem_parent_runtime_fallback:<ExcType>); missing build-time references return an empty mapping, a concise setup-failure category that leaves the parent installed. No inputs/previous-feedback.txt and no inputs/previous-candidate/ exist, so this is the first attempt with nothing to reconcile. Optional tunable stem_chunk_rows (default 8) lets the TaskSearch/TPE loop trade launch overhead for stem transient without touching frozen semantics; chunk 4 keeps the ~168.8 MB stage tier with 8 chunks, chunk 16 halves launches at ~194.5 MB stem-limited peak (46,758,048 + 19,267,584 + 25,690,112 + 2x51,380,224) - both still far below baseline.

quality_risks: Numerics: cudnn may select a different conv1 kernel at batch 8, reordering the 147-term accumulation and producing ulp-level logits differences; quality requires full 1000-class logits within atol=rtol=1e-4 and exact top-1 - expected to hold comfortably (BatchNorm(eval)/ReLU/MaxPool are value-exact under row chunking and a CPU replica of the composition is bit-identical), but only the evaluator's reference comparison against offline-reference semantics decides

Throughput: if batch-8 scudnn efficiency loss plus the 4x launch and assembly-copy overhead exceeds the +224 us headroom over the 4.2465 ms baseline, images_per_second could fall below the 7158.9 floor; the declared stem_chunk_rows=16 parameter is the fallback (2 chunks, fewer launches, ~194.5 MB peak) and is itself a large memory improvement over baseline

Fallback semantics: any exception inside the chunked path re-executes the whole stem through the parent reference (idempotent under eval/inference_mode, no state mutated) and self-reports stem_parent_runtime_fallback:<type>; guards route unexpected signatures, kwargs, non-contiguous/odd-dtype/CPU/requires-grad inputs and training mode to the parent with stem_parent_signature_fallback, so adversarial or unseen calls preserve exact parent behavior

Coverage: the only replaced boundary is the stem module; all 17 selection-listed stem-subtree call IDs keep executing (subtree invocation count 1->4 per invocation at chunk 8), so quality coverage and runtime traces still observe the inherited conv/bn/relu/maxpool work; no calls are eliminated and no counter is filled with unused work

selection.rationale: Objective peak_allocated_bytes on the current accepted version (stem micro-batch rows8 + stage-0 micro-batch rows8, both verified executing in this discovery: stem Conv2d/BatchNorm2d/ReLU/max_pool2d n=4, copy_ n=4, one 32x64x56x56 assembly; stage-0 slices/Sequential/Identity n=4, add_ n=8) measures exactly 177,409,024 B = live FP32 params 46,758,048 + GPU-resident input 19,267,584 + retained workspace 8,622,944 + 4 x 25,690,112, where 25,690,112 is one 32x64x56x56 FP32 unit (also exactly 8x64x112x112). The previous parameter search measured stage0_chunk_rows=8 and =16 at the identical 177,409,024, so the binding moment is independent of stage-0 chunk transients; the peak now sits in a phase that parameter cannot touch. Static liveness bounds leave the unchanged stage-1 phase at <= base + 1 unit + 3-4 x 12,845,056 and the chunked stage-0 phase at ~ base + 2 units + 6,422,528 transients, both below the measured 4 units; the stem phase is the only phase where 3 x 25,690,112 coexist in the observed aten sequence (full assembly empty+4x copy_, chunk conv_out 8x64x112x112, chunk bn_out 8x64x112x112), with the fourth unit unexplained by static shapes (per-operator allocation attribution is an explicit unknown; plausibly cudnn workspace for the 7x7 stride-2 conv, which also scales with chunk rows). Halving the stem chunk is the one lever that shrinks every term of that phase: rows=4 turns conv_out/bn_out (and any row-scaled workspace) into 12,845,056 each while the assembly stays 25,690,112. The earlier stem parameter search already executed rows=4 cleanly (objective identical to rows=8 at 203,099,136 while stage 0 was binding), so the lever is proven executable and quality-passing. Selection: region scope re-binding the ResNetEmbeddings boundary (call d16297b8a11b79a2657853d0) with the same proven pattern at half chunk size, running the unchanged Conv2d/BatchNorm2d/ReLU/max_pool parents through context.references on contiguous row chunks and assembling one [32,64,56,56] FP32 tensor consumed unchanged by the untouched stage-0 bundle and stages 1-3; no functional dispatch sites, so the legacy direct-callable backend applies. All 32 stem-subtree groups are selected; the 49 additional calls (stage-0 assembly empty/copy_/slice calls and 43 record_function_exit family calls) are included only because those group families share ownership across the region boundary, matching the accepted region-selection precedent.
selection.hypothesis: Re-binding the stem region at chunk_rows=4 (parameter space may probe 2/4/8) lowers peak_allocated_bytes from 177,409,024 B to approximately 151,718,912 B (-25,690,112, -14.5%): with 4-row chunks the stem-phase coexistence becomes assembly 25,690,112 + conv_out 12,845,056 + bn_out 12,845,056 + one further <=25,690,112 term (the statically unexplained unit, likely conv workspace that itself shrinks with rows), i.e. base 74,648,576 + 2 x 25,690,112 + 2 x 12,845,056 at worst. Even if the unexplained unit is fixed-size, the arithmetic lands exactly on 151,718,912; the graceful floor is the unchanged stage-0 phase (~145.3 MB: stage input + assembled output + 6,422,528 transients) and stage-1 phase (~151.4 MB), so no gain below ~145 MB is claimed. Throughput: constraint is images_per_second >= 7,158.9 (0.95 x 7535.66); the accepted version measured 8,506-8,538 img/s (16-19% headroom), rows=4 only adds four extra small conv/bn/relu/pool launches versus the accepted rows=8 route, and stem chunking has previously measured throughput-neutral, so the constraint is expected to hold. Numerics: identical per-sample FP32 kernels (eval batch_norm, out-of-place relu, max_pool2d, conv2d) on contiguous batch slices, the pattern already accepted twice with max_abs_error 7.6e-06 within atol=rtol=1e-4 and exact top-1; full 1000-class logits and predicted classes are unchanged. The installed stage-0 bundle trial-fd9bdc62a2-param-b6738601 is untouched and composes unchanged: it consumes the same [32,64,56,56] FP32 tensor this boundary returns. How previous-feedback shapes this attempt: trial-fd9bdc62a2 was ACCEPTED (quality pass, max_abs_error 7.6e-06, exact top-1, objective 177,409,024 vs parent 203,099,136, paired AB/BA with zero noise; coverage routes stem_microbatch_rows8 and stage0_microbatch_rows8 both verified with 8/8 reference invocations), so there is no rejected implementation to repair. The one concrete failure recorded in the feedback is the stage0_chunk_rows=4 screening endpoint violating the throughput floor (6,854.59 img/s vs limit 7,158.88). This attempt responds to that failure rather than repeating it: the targeted region is the stem, an order of magnitude smaller than stage 0 (per target-resources the whole stem phase is 552.3 us of CUDA over 20 kernels at rows=8: conv 321.6 + bn 80.0 + relu 63.0 + maxpool 87.7, versus stage 0's two full BasicLayers), whose rows=4 route already executed cleanly and quality-passed in the earlier stem parameter search; and the parameter domain is restricted to [4, 8] with 8 as the proven-safe point, deliberately excluding rows=2 because the static memory floors of the unchanged phases (~145.3 MB stage-0 phase, ~151.4 MB stage-1 phase) mean rows=2 cannot beat the rows=4 plateau while multiplying exactly the launch-efficiency loss that invalidated the stage-0 rows=4 endpoint.
